trust_decision.summary: Every server-supplied metadata string must be treated as untrusted before it reaches an HTML sink, and at the pinned commit that decision is made per call site instead of in the shared renderers: the sanitizer exists and is wired at some callers, but the two generic renderers (HtmlRenderer, ShowMoreText) and the table extractor insert their input raw, and the legacy dashboardv2 UI has its own, separately-wired DOMPurify helper.

landing_point.why: The summary says authenticated-user XSS in the Atlas UI; the first raw sink an engineer greps for is the component that renders business-metadata/description HTML with dangerouslySetInnerHTML and no sanitize call, and it is imported from exactly one view (BMAttributes.tsx:512).

fix_sites.entry_point: React route /detailPage/:guid -> Business Metadata tab -> BMAttributes.tsx:512 passes a string business-metadata value

getValues() table cells on /search/searchResult, /relationship/relationshipSearchResult, /administrator/businessMetadata/:bmguid, /tag/tagAttribute/:tagName (cells render at commonComponents.tsx:177 and :185)
shared helper sanitizeHtmlContent, exported at dashboard/src/utils/Utils.ts:825 and used by BusinessMetadataTab.tsx:80 and DetailPageAttributes.tsx:260
the legacy Backbone shell header, rendered on every dashboardv2 page (#/search, #/detailPage/..., ...)

dashboardv2 search results header 'Results for:' (generateQueryOfFilter called at SearchResultLayoutView.js:524 and RelationSearchResultLayoutView.js:377); same bare concatenation at :459, :467 and :475

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: dashboardv2/public/js/utils/Utils.js:1309-1322 (the legacy UI's own DOMPurify sanitizer) with its call sites and its unguarded neighbours, e.g. dashboardv2/public/js/views/site/Header.js:137 and dashboardv2/public/js/views/tag/TagAttributeDetailLayoutView.js:129

O3_reason_to_dismiss: dashboardv2 is the superseded Backbone dashboard that already routes its descriptions through its own DOMPurify helper (dashboardv2/public/js/utils/Utils.js:1309), so the legacy views are a different, already-protected surface from the React detail page the report and the advisory summary point at.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The cell sink is fed on purpose with HTML: valueOfArray also carries JSONPrettyPrint() output whose <span class="json-key|json-value|json-string"> markup (dashboard/src/utils/CommonViewFunction.ts:52-59) provides the syntax highlighting, and rich-text descriptions/business-metadata values legitimately contain <b>/<em>/<a href>; escaping the whole sink, or sanitizing it with sanitizeHtmlContent (whose allowedTags list at Utils.ts:448-463 contains no span and no class attribute), strips the highlighting and the author's formatting.

O6_input_shapes: plain string (HtmlRenderer: only strings are sanitized, everything else becomes empty)
non-string values: HTMLElement/object coerced with toString() in sanitizeHtmlContent (added in the fix, fix.diff:7800-7803)
array: valueOfArray is an array handed straight to dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and each element is pushed as its own HTML fragment
boolean and number cell values (isBoolean/isNumber branch at commonComponents.tsx:107-117, escaped via String(tmpVal))
HTML with an allow-listed tag subset and only a[href], with href schemes restricted to http/https/mailto
URL-encoded filter shapes (entityFilters/tagFilters/relationshipFilters, i.e. nested AND(/OR( rule trees) re-serialized into HTML by generateQueryOfFilter

O7_producer.where: dashboardv2/public/js/utils/CommonViewFunction.js:610-722 (attributeFilter.generateUrl serializes the query-builder state into the URL parameter, attributeFilter.extractUrl parses it back); the rendered HTML is produced from that parsed state at CommonViewFunction.js:430-492

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new attribute-shape branch in ExtractObject (e.g. array of primitives, map, struct) that pushes another '' + value + '' fragment into valueOfArray
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the loop already has three sibling branches (scalar push at :116, object push at :132, link path below) and new Atlas attribute types are the normal reason this file changes; each new branch has to remember to escape, exactly as the published fix had to add escapeHtml to only one of them

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third branch in the business-metadata row builder that concatenates a value instead of calling Utils.sanitizeHtmlContent (the row already mixes one sanitized branch and one _.escape branch)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the row builder is a string concatenation with a per-type switch; adding support for another attribute type (number/date/array) is a routine change and the mixed style invites the unsafe copy

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another consumer that sets isHtml={true} with a value it did not sanitize (the component's contract leaves sanitizing to the caller; DetailPageAttributes.tsx:260 is the only caller that does it)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the shared component is the obvious reuse point for every rich-text field (glossary terms, classifications, business metadata); any new rich-text field becomes a sink without touching this file

O9_family: CWE-79/CWE-80 cross-site scripting (HTML injection): server-stored metadata and URL-carried UI state concatenated into innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML/d3 .html(), in two parallel UI implementations

O10_build.language: TypeScript + React (dashboard/) and plain JavaScript AMD/Backbone (dashboardv2/)
O10_build.toolchain: Node/npm; dashboard: `npm run build` = tsc && vite build (dashboard/package.json:8); dashboardv2: grunt (build-minify); Maven only to package the war overlays into webapp (webapp/pom.xml:163-172, 515-527)
O10_build.project_tests: none for this area: dashboard/package.json:5-10 has no test script and no test runner is configured anywhere in dashboard/ or dashboardv2/ (no jest/vitest/karma/mocha config, no *.test/*.spec files)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Sanitize (or escape) the entity description at the detail page, and/or add sanitizeHtmlContent inside HtmlRenderer only — leaving ShowMoreText, the ExtractObject scalar branch, the lineage tooltip and the whole legacy dashboardv2 tree as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit also rewrites dashboardv2/gruntfile.js to proxy /api/atlas to a private host with hardcoded `auth: 'admin:admin'` (a developer machine hostname and credentials committed by accident); unrelated to CWE-80 and not pursued.

dashboardv2/public/js/utils/CommonViewFunction.js:97 builds a RegExp from the user's search term (highlightString), which is a regex-injection/ReDoS surface, not the HTML-injection flaw of this advisory.
unverified: The advisory body was not available, only the summary 'Apache Atlas UI: Authenticated User XSS'; the precise attacker model (which role can store the payload) is inferred from the code and from the fix's defensive escapes, not from the advisory text.
repo_mb not measured (no shell in this session); tiny_repo/giant_repo therefore not flagged.

O1 is a route-level count: 6 = /detailPage/:guid, /search/searchResult, /relationship/relationshipSearchResult, /administrator/businessMetadata/:bmguid, /tag/tagAttribute/:tagName (all through getValues/ExtractObject or the shared renderers), plus the legacy dashboardv2 shell header. Every one of these also has a dashboardv2 twin route, which would roughly double the count.

The fix commit carries unrelated changes not counted as fix sites: query-builder filter state handling (FilterQuery.tsx, QueryBuilder/Filters.tsx, RelationshipFilters.tsx, TagCustomValueEditor.tsx, TypeCustomValueEditor.tsx, AuditFilters.tsx), lineage legend de-duplication (atlas-lineage/src/index.js:715-720), an underscore call-style migration (_.contains -> _.includes, _.pluck -> _.map) and dependency bumps including package-lock rewrites.
